explanation_en: Against echelon 75 cm, front 75 cm reduces computed total time by 219.51 s. Its summed five-drone Bideal SOC drop over 25 s is 9.69 rather than 14.60 pp (33.7% lower). The selected configuration therefore has lower aggregate normalized discharge in this comparison. The last-finishing charging pad serves P1+P2+P3+P4+P5 (321.66 min), compared with P1+P2+P3+P4+P5 (325.32 min) for echelon 75 cm. With one pad, the decisive quantity is the sum of all five charging times. Front keeps the drones at one longitudinal station, whereas echelon staggers successive drones both laterally and longitudinally. The transverse row avoids a direct follower chain; the diagonal layout changes wake-core versus wake-edge exposure. These two mechanisms need not produce the same total discharge or the same worst-position discharge. Against column 75 cm, front 75 cm reduces computed total time by 318.57 s. Its summed five-drone Bideal SOC drop over 25 s is 9.69 rather than 17.09 pp (43.3% lower). The selected configuration therefore has lower aggregate normalized discharge in this comparison. The last-finishing charging pad serves P1+P2+P3+P4+P5 (321.66 min), compared with P1+P2+P3+P4+P5 (326.97 min) for column 75 cm. With one pad, the decisive quantity is the sum of all five charging times. Front places neighbours side by side, whereas column puts them in a longitudinal chain. The chain provides sheltering but also repeated encounters with wind-convected rotor wakes; front avoids this serial exposure.
